itemListElement.name: How Immigrant Communities Choose a Local Business (and Why Your Ads Miss Them)

mainEntity.name: How do immigrant customers choose a local business?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single answer, and no public study describes every community. A useful working model is a chain of trust: a recommendation from someone they know, a check of reviews and the profile, and a call or message that shows whether the business can understand them. Test that chain against your own customers by asking how they found you.

mainEntity.name: Do immigrant customers search for local businesses on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some do, but for a customer who was given a name, search is often a step to verify it. For that reason, your Google Business Profile, your reviews and the language on your page matter even when the first contact came from a person.

mainEntity.name: Should I get reviews in Spanish or other languages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if your customers speak them. Tell happy customers they can write in the language they prefer, and reply in the language of each review. Never offer a discount or a gift in exchange for a review, because Google prohibits it.

mainEntity.name: Is a contact form enough for a customer who is not fluent in English?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is rarely the best option on its own. A phone number that someone answers, and a WhatsApp option you actually check, give the customer a way to explain and ask questions, which is where trust forms.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to translate my whole website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not as a first step. Start by checking who answers the phone and what your reviews and Google profile say. Then publish one well-written service page for the language you want to reach, instead of machine translating everything.
